text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Representatives of demonstrating farmers drove tractors to Parliament at noon on Tuesday and presented a 14-point petition to Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal. Police reported 120 demonstrations across the country, as against 150 the previous day.
- Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will arrive in Budapest today at the head of a large delegation of Romanian cabinet members and businessmen.

- Parliament placed on its urgent agenda an amendment to the laws on taxation, social insurance and social care affecting agricultural workers. Later Parliament amended the law on mining and endorsed a bill on trademark protection.
- The Ministry of Labour is seeking to amend the labour code despite reservations from employers.
- Rectors from four universities appealed in a letter to the minister of culture to guarantee funds for the payment of public servant salary increases.
- Domestic investment funds were handling HUF 151 billion as of early March.
- Consumer prices in February were 2.2 percent higher than in the previous month.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- General Motors is planning to purchase components and car parts from Central Europe to a total value of $1 billion by the end of the century, said head of General Motors Europe Richard Donnelly.
- Merrill Lynch forecasts a three-to-five year period of growth for the pgharmaceuticals company Richter Gedeon Rt., the paper reported, citing Wall Street Journal Europe.

- The paper reports that the two governing parties agree with the basic principles of a planned amendment to the electoral law, notably those aimed at reducing the length of the campaign period and placing limits on campaign funding.
- The government's national agricultural programme will be presented to the parliamentary parties and agricultural interest groups at an agricultural conference in Godollo on Thursday.

- Import-related obligations are expected to drop 10 percent this year due to agreements with the EU and other free trade zones, in line with the growing number of free trade agreements worldwide. The Hungarian foreign trade deficit may grow due to the changes, analysts said.
- Three bids for the purchase of the assets of the Northern Hungarian Chemical Works have been received by the company's liquidator.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Socialist Executive Vice-President Magda Kovacs has been appointed responsible for media relations and Socialist Party media policy.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs will pay an official visit to Bonn on March 17-18.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Hungarian government has requested a $225 million World Bank loan for the reconstruction of the domestic corporate and financial sector.
NEPSZAVA
- The Dutch banking group ING is to invest more than HUF 5 billion in its Hungarian businesses.
- The two-storey Europark, the third shopping mall in Budapest, opened in the capital's 19th district on Tuesday.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
